F01: Why this work; what changed; what should stop?
F02: What exists, runs, gets used and remains unknown?
F03: Which facts count and which decisions need review?
F04: What can a cold successor safely continue?
F05: Which arrangement meets privacy, quality and urgency?
F06: Who may do this, for whom, within which limits?
F07: Was it claimed, executed, observed and accepted?
F08: What is committed, enforced, spent or unknown?
F09: Can the whole application recover without duplicate effects?
F10: What entered the workflow and where could it go?
F11: Which change improved useful outcomes with sufficient evidence?
F12: What needs my judgment and how do I recover?
F13: Can another provider or person continue with intact meaning?
F14: What changed in the household, creative or research domain?

obstacles: Stale configuration mistaken for observed reality
Session loss, duplicate message or late report corrupts settlement
Cheap inference causes expensive retries or contention
Tool content or successor identity amplifies authority
Self-report or model grader substitutes for acceptance
Partial restore or uncertain effect is blindly retried
Biased cohorts/sparse capture imply false improvement
Swap loses hidden session state or evidence meaning
Fixture success substitutes for actual household/play outcome

activities.title: Define and implement durable operator-request contract
activities.work: Ratify canonical coordination ownership and API alongside existing work/effect owners; implement stable identity, revision-safe updates, multiple requesting sessions and work dependencies, typed perform/authorize/decide/provide-information requests, complete versioned procedures, freshness and withdrawal semantics. No new effect authority or independent work-status ledger.
activities.acceptance: Duplicate retries create one request; concurrent revisions conflict explicitly; one requester withdrawing preserves other dependants; dead sessions retain requests with uncertain freshness; material command/target/authority changes invalidate prior acceptance; unavailable source is not completed or withdrawn.

activities.title: Integrate Claude and Codex request publication and reconciliation
activities.work: Implement shared CLI/MCP publishing contract through qualified native-runtime integrations; verify genuine operator blockers; publish complete instructions before yielding; update or withdraw stable requests; use non-authoritative retry outbox during outages. Qualify each local/cloud/runtime mode separately. Transcript extraction may suggest candidates only.
activities.acceptance: Both Claude and Codex publish and revise requests with session/project/workspace/host links; retry/reconnect deduplicates; unsupported modes are explicit; routine permitted work is not handed off; raw logs and secrets are excluded; session closure is not completion.

activities.title: Deliver operator-action TUI over shared request lifecycle
activities.work: Build keyboard-first collated TUI with ready/revalidation/verification/deferred views, impact and context filters, complete multi-step procedures, exact host/cwd/identity/target, expected results, progress and recovery, source-session links, defer/decline/report-performed actions. Reuse shared owner API and per-workspace entitlements.
activities.acceptance: Operator completes a request without reopening chat; wrong-host/stale-revision requests cannot appear ready; procedure progress survives restart; unauthorized project data is absent; viewing/copying or reporting performed is not authorization or successful effect; sensitive values remain outside durable request content.

activities.title: Verify operator outcomes and deliver safe continuation events
activities.work: Implement explicit completion basis (authorized source observation or human attestation), partial/uncertain result reconciliation, versioned resolution events and retry-safe delivery; integrate through native-runtime owners for wake/resume or explicit continuation-ready packets. Scope blocked work precisely and support successor takeover without introducing a scheduler.
activities.acceptance: A false performed report remains unverified; physical work can resolve with labeled human attestation; multiple dependants receive one logical resolution; lost/duplicate delivery never repeats an effect; unavailable native wake produces visible continuation-ready state; a successor continues from current work and exact evidence without original chat.

activities.title: Add shared web view and bounded operator notifications
activities.work: Reuse qualified request API for web UI; add assignment, defer-until/change conditions, explicit deadlines and bounded notification preferences. Batch compatible contexts while retaining independent authority boundaries; show coverage and freshness across runtimes. Qualify notification and identity integrations rather than duplicating native approval controls.
activities.acceptance: TUI/web show consistent revisions; unauthorized tenant data never leaks; unchanged requests remain quiet; meaningful changes re-surface appropriately; defer and decline propagate to affected work; expired action instructions require refresh; partial runtime coverage is visible.

activities.title: Qualify overnight operator-action workflow across both runtimes
activities.work: Run real interactive authentication, multi-step operator procedure and explicit authorization workflows with Claude and Codex; include dead requester, shared request, stale target, partial failure, missed wake and another session completing work. Compare against predeclared AO-K02 attention baseline; document setup, support, upgrade, rollback and export.
activities.acceptance: After an overnight absence the operator acts from one current list without reconstructing chats; affected work resumes or explicitly becomes continuation-ready; all mandatory negative cases pass; report denominators, stale/unnecessary requests, repeated prompts, operator effort, human wait and post-resolution delay. Retain/revise/adopt decision uses evidence, not screen availability.
